Waterfalls pour off the floating island's edge in long ribbons, dissolving into mist as they fall into the empty cloud far below.
Great rusted chains hang from the castle's underside, trailing down into the void, anchored to nothing visible beneath the clouds.
Smaller chunks of rock drift slowly around the main island, each trailing its own tiny garden of hanging vines and pale flowers.
Long arching sky-bridges span the gaps between tower and tower, their stone worn smooth by constant high wind and dragon claws.
Crystal anchors the size of houses glow with pale blue light at each corner of the island, humming faintly in the cold air.
Enormous banners stream horizontally in the relentless wind, their colors faded but their fabric impossibly intact after countless years aloft.
Gardens cascade over the island's rim in great curtains of green, roots dangling freely in open sky, fed only by cloud and magic.
Glowing runes carved into the bedrock beneath the castle pulse with amber light, the ancient words that keep the whole mass airborne.
A spiral staircase winds around the entire underside of the island, its steps carved directly into the rock, leading nowhere anyone remembers.
Airship docks jut from the eastern cliff face, their wooden platforms creaking, old mooring ropes fraying and snapping in the gusting wind.
A single beam of blinding white light descends from the castle's heart straight down through the clouds, tethering it to something far below.
Thick roots and hanging vines trail hundreds of feet beneath the island, swaying slowly, brushing the tops of cloudbanks like enormous fingers.
A ring of smaller floating rocks orbits the castle at mid-height, each one spinning slightly as it circles in its slow eternal path.
The underside of the island is encrusted with enormous pale stalactites, each one carved with faces that watch the world below in silence.
Broken towers hang inverted from the island's belly, their foundations in the rock above, their shattered tops pointing down into open sky.
A vast hourglass of iron and glass stands at the island's peak, its sand pouring upward impossibly, glowing gold against the dark clouds.
Rope bridges of ancient braided dragonhide swing between outlying rock formations, each one marked with warning runes near its swaying center span.
Fountains on the upper terraces spill water over the edge in wide sheets, the falling water catching sunlight into brief rainbows before vanishing.
A graveyard clings to the island's most precarious edge, its tilted headstones overlooking nothing but open sky and the tops of distant mountains.
Enormous iron bells hang beneath the main tower, ringing without pause in the high wind, their deep tones rolling out across empty miles.
A network of copper pipes winds across the outer walls, venting steam in rhythmic bursts, part of some mechanism that still runs below.
The outer walls are overgrown with luminous moss that glows soft green at night, making the whole castle visible from leagues away in darkness.
Collapsed sections of outer wall have become natural perches for wind-spirits, their translucent forms roosting in the broken stone like enormous pale birds.
Great iron rings are set into the cliff faces all around the island, sized for chains that no longer hang there, their purpose forgotten.
At the island's lowest point a single massive stalactite extends far below all others, its tip carved into the open mouth of a dragon.
